5
A projectile is launched at an angle of 25 to the horizontal with a horizontal component of
velocity of 13 m s–1.
What is the vertical component of the velocity of the projectile when it is launched?
A
5.5 m s–1
B
6.1 m s–1
C
12 m s–1
D
14 m s–1

hints: Draw the launch velocity triangle with angle $25^{\circ}$ to the horizontal: the given $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is the adjacent side and the wanted vertical component is the opposite side.
Recall that opposite over adjacent is $\tan \theta$, so vertical component $= 13 \tan 25^{\circ}$.
Check that the vertical side must be much smaller than $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because $25^{\circ}$ is a shallow angle, then evaluate $13 \times \tan 25^{\circ}$.
walkthrough: Identify the right-angled velocity triangle at launch: angle $25^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, adjacent $v_x = 13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, opposite $v_y = ?$.
State the trigonometric rule: $\tan \theta = v_y / v_x$, so $v_y = v_x \tan \theta$.
Calculate the intermediate value: $\tan 25^{\circ} \approx 0.4663$, so $v_y \approx 13 \times 0.4663 \approx 6.06 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Check units and sense: result is in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ and smaller than $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, as expected for a $25^{\circ}$ launch. Rounded to two significant figures this is $6.1 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Too small for $13 \tan 25^{\circ}$. It comes from using $13 \sin 25^{\circ}$ instead of relating vertical to horizontal.

C.explanation: Close to $13 \cos 25^{\circ}$. That treats $13 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ as the full launch speed, not the horizontal component.

D.explanation: Close to $13 / \cos 25^{\circ}$. That calculates the full launch speed $v$, not the vertical component $v \sin 25^{\circ}$.
